title: The Context Window — the only budget that matters

questions.prompt: Halfway through a long session you need to make sure one rule holds for the next two hours of work. Where does it belong?
options: In the conversation, restated every few turns so the agent keeps seeing it
In CLAUDE.md at the project root
At the top of the file the agent will edit next
In the first message of the session, since context is stored oldest-first
questions.explanation: Compaction summarizes older history, so a rule that lives only in conversation is exactly what gets summarized away — and restating it just refills the window you are trying to protect. CLAUDE.md is re-injected from disk after compaction, which is the whole reason it is the durable place for a rule. Option C is seductive but wrong: a file's contents only enter context when it is read, and only that reading gets summarized away. Option D inverts the mechanism — nothing in the window is priority-ordered.

questions.prompt: You finished a refactor and are starting an unrelated feature in the same repo. /context shows the window more than half full. What is the right move?
options: Keep going — the window has room and clearing loses the refactor's reasoning
Run /compact with a focus note, so the old work is summarized rather than dropped
Run /clear with a name, so the new feature starts in an empty window
Ask the agent to ignore the earlier part of the conversation
questions.explanation: Unrelated work does not benefit from the previous task's history — it only competes for window space and is re-paid on every turn. /clear starts the new task empty and /resume can bring the old thread back if you need it. Option B is for continuing the same task, where the history still has value. Option D asks for something the harness decides, not the model — compaction is not something a request can turn off.

questions.prompt: The window is at roughly 80% and the agent still needs to read four more files. What is the most useful thing to do before asking for those reads?
options: Run /context, find the largest non-conversation category, and see whether it is something you actually needed
Ask the agent to work faster so it generates fewer output tokens
Switch to a model with a smaller context window to leave headroom
Nothing — the harness compacts automatically, so there is no decision to make
questions.explanation: /context shows the window broken down by category, so you can find out what is actually large before deciding what to do about it — that is the decision worth making. Option A's wrong turn is assuming the conversation is the problem; often it is one large file read or one command output. Option C inverts the goal: a smaller window makes the squeeze worse. Option D is half true — automatic compaction is real, but it decides what to drop for you, which is exactly the loss you are trying to avoid.
